Can someone please tell me why this is fake? There are a lot of suspect things that I can see, but nothing that I can point out as definitive.

I'm no ballistics expert, but I'm pretty sure mannequins don't blow up when you shoot them. Also, it seems that the drone has exceptional attitude control considering the fact that it seems to be laying down 5 or 6 round bursts of automatic fire. Sure, there's recoil, but it looks off. Also, where's the ammo feed? I see no magazine.

Waiting for someone who knows what they're talking about to come in and tell me why I'm wrong.

If you watch the drone closely it has some unnatural characteristics. For instance when it shoots out the back window and enters the car, it looks animated. Secondly I'm no wizard but from the dimensions of the first close up shot, it's physically too big to smoothly transition into the car, the window also breaks too completely.

Also watch him 'fly' the drone. The movements don't coordinate. For a loaded weapon he let's the barrel swing over him and the camera quite a bit.

Lots of stuff gives it away.

1) Those rotors are barely enough to lift a camera let alone a machine gun with ammunition.

2) The way the drone moves is totally unrealistic, it does this slow wobble thing that actual drones don't do because if they're not as still as possible they fly all over the place and are impossible to control. When it's shooting you can see it's angling down, the rotors are aligned with the body also facing down, yet it stays still in the air. In real life a drone in that position would be flying down towards the mannequins like it was on a water slide.

3) The recoil is way, way too light and it's regaining control and aiming way too quickly. Refer to the real video of the drone with the handgun and you'll see how just one shot throws the whole thing off and it has to readjust. Especially controlling it from a tablet, it would take much longer to readjust your aim.

4) There's also some slightly-off tracking between the 3D CGI drone and the background footage so if you look closely you can tell it looks unnatural. What I would have done is flown the real drone and mimicked the action of the shooting and then later added the muzzle flashes and spliced it into the exploding mannequins footage. If you filmed it all from a tripod and kept the camera still you could easily patch them together and then mimic the handheld camera movement later.

So yeah, there's a lot of things that are wrong with the video that are more obvious when you compare side by side with actual drone footage.
If you look at the gun, it's just a barrel and handgaurd from an AR-15. Not an actual weapon, just part of it.

First of all it's CGI; that's a dead give-away. Second, that "sub machine gun" doesn't have any receiver, which means no bolt and no way to feed ammo into it; there's some hose that obviously serves no purpose. Third, the bullets that are hitting the ground are coming from a totally different angle and the recoil of the gun when it "fires" is totally unnatural. Fourth, the amount of dust that it kicks up is absolutely tiny compared to what a comparably sized drone would produce, and when it flied and hovers over the ground, there is zero dust. Also, the rotors don't interact with the smoke from the explosions.

I'm curious as I'd love a dual monitor setup but display port is just another useless adapter.
What is display port and why do man GFX cards come with more display ports than HDMI often 3:1? I thought HDMI is not only king, but by a lot.

It's not. Not only has DP an higher bandwidth, it's actually powerful enough to feed multiple screens with monitor hubs or via daisy-chaining. (21.6 Gbit/s for DP and 10.2 Gbit/s for HDMI) If you have the screens and PC that can handle it, it basically means more FPS and a bigger resolution. Though most people don't have good enough screens to see a noticeable change.

On the contrary, Display port is the way to go. Not only does it have more bandwidth as /u/wouldntsavezion was talking about, but adapters are cheap and pretty much universal. I can get a displayport to just about any other type of video connection adapter out there. Also, displayport is a shit-tonne more cheaper to make compared to HDMI:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DisplayPort#Advantages_over_DVI.2C_VGA_and_FPD-Link
